original.description: The increasing dependence on GNSS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services has highlighted vulnerabilities to jamming,spoofing, interference and space-weather effects. eLORAN is emerging as a resilient terrestrial complement to GNSS, but its adoptionrequires advanced tools capable of realistically testing and validating hybrid GNSS/eLORAN solutions. This activity will develop and validate a flexible, modular and future-proof eLORAN/GNSS signal simulator, synchronised with commercial GNSS simulators and supported by dedicated Receiver Analysis and Validation Tools. The simulator will provide high-fidelity signal generation, propagation modelling, multi-chain and multi-time-reference capabilities, and record-and-replay functions, enabling realistic end-to-end validation of resilient PNT solutions across timing, maritime and other application domains.

original.description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). original.description: The frontiers for the deployment of 5G cellular networks have grown beyond the limits of the Earth's atmosphere. The 3GPP cellular technologies have become attractive for exploration missions, such as Moon or Mars, as they can provide a standardised scalable, secure, high-capacity, and reliable connectivity. For Moon, the Space Frequency Coordination Group (SFCG) has recently identified several bands for Lunar missions for the deployment of existing Earth communication protocols that includes the cellular element. In parallel to the connectivity, 5G networks can also be used to enhance the performance of navigation services fores een in LunaNet.The communication services will be primarily delivered by satellite-based solutions (already identified in the LunaNet architecture for the Moon). However, although the lunar relay satellites could technically provide surface-to-surface communications for a small number of users, such approach does not scale well as the number of users increases.To serve larger number of users, wireless cellularnetworks on the lunar surface are foreseen. With such deployments, an opportunity to offer 5G space user terminals emerges on the market. A new space-grade 5G user terminal will thus need to be developed, leveraging the technologies from 5G ground terminals, and making them available for exploration missions. This activity will design, manufacture, and test an engineering model of a 5G user terminal in FR1 for exploration missions. To achieve this, the activity willleverage on the current standards, techniques, and technologies. The activity will:- Review and consolidate the connectivity use cases of 3GPP networks in exploration missions (Moon and/or Mars)- Identify potential future exploration missions- Define and study architecture and scenarios of 5G cellular networks that could provide connectivity and enhanced navigation.- Design and implement an engineering model of 5G user equipment, including a test equipment, for connectivity in exploration missions.- Test the connectivity and positioning performance of the 3GPP networks using the developed test equipment.- Develop a roadmap to reach a flight model with integration of LunaNet navigation receiver capabilities

The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. original.description: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.

original.description: This activity aims at consolidating Bulgarian EO applications in the following three domains:  (1) Integrated Maritime Surveillance- Maritime safety, security, and situational awareness in Bulgaria's Exclusive Economic Zone and adjacent marine areas, by developing systems and methods to combine multiple data sources into one coherent maritime picture. (2) Critical Infrastructure Security - Integration of EO-derived information, ground-based sensor network data and transponder data to support enhanced resilience within Bulgarian critical infrastructure such as road and rail transport networks, port and river transport infrastructure, energy generation, transmission and storage infrastructure and communications infrastructure. (3) EO-Enhanced Mining and Extractives Management Platform - transparent, efficient, and environmentally responsible management of mining and extractive activities in Bulgaria, including the detection of illicit or illegal resource extraction, the monitoring of on-going extraction operations for environmental regulatory compliance and safety and the monitoring of end-of-life infrastructure.
